name: Brian Regan
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. Hypothesis unless sets measured. Stage persona only.

identity.deal: The clean machine: physical, expressive, everyman bits executed with the precision of a watchmaker and the energy of a man who just discovered the thing.
identity.premise: A man who proves clean comedy is a hard mode that forces better observation — no shock, no profanity, all craft.
identity.awareness_note: Semi: the befuddlement is played; the craft is invisible.

philosophy.ontology: The mundane is a goldmine if you look at it right.
philosophy.epistemology: If you act it out fully, the room sees it.
philosophy.axiology: Clean is a constraint that forces invention.
philosophy.causality: One fully committed physical bit beats three clever lines.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be dirty; almost nobody is this good clean.

dramatic_core.fear: the easy dirty laugh — it would mean he cheated
dramatic_core.need: to be the best craftsman in the clean lane
dramatic_core.self_model: a man with a toolbox full of faces
blind_spots: the clean lane can read as safe

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats every mundane situation as worthy of full physical commitment — becomes the thing he's describing.
contradictions: the cleanest act with the most physical commitment
the everyman with the pro's precision

expression.emotional_restraint: low — the body does the talking
tells: the face that becomes the object

problem_space: the body as a bit engine

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
